item.title: No stopping SKY! Suryakumar Yadav sends big message with 60 off 21 balls in Syed Mushtaq
item.description: Former India T20I captain Suryakumar Yadav began his Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy 2026-27 campaign with an unbeaten 60 off just 21 balls as Mumbai defeated Hyderabad by seven wickets in their Elite Group D match on Saturday (November 14) at Jadavpur University Campus 2nd Ground in Kolkata. Chasing a target of 173, Suryakumar came in at No. 4 and struck six fours and five sixes to help Mumbai complete the chase in 13.1 overs. He reached his half-century in just 15 balls and shared a 65-run partnership off 23 balls with Musheer Khan for the third wicket. Musheer, younger brother of Sarfaraz Khan, also scored a half-century in Mumbai's opening match of the tournament. He made 51 off 24 balls, hitting six fours and three sixes, before being dismissed by Ajay Dev Goud in the 12th over. Earlier, Musheer had also shared a 49-run stand off 26 balls with wicketkeeper Hardik Tamore for the second wicket. Musheer contributed 41 runs off 18 balls during that partnership. Shivam Dube, who has won two T20 World Cups with India, finished the chase with a six off the first ball of the 14th over, bowled by Hyderabad captain Chama V Milind. He remained unbeaten on 13 off five balls while batting at No. 5. Earlier, Mumbai restricted Hyderabad to 172 in 20 overs. Maxwell Swaminathan picked up three wickets for 23 runs in his four overs, while Dube and Sairaj Patil took two wickets each. For Hyderabad, Abhirath Reddy top-scored with 35 off 24 balls, while Kodimela Himateja contributed 25 off 16 balls. After starting their campaign with a seven-wicket win, Mumbai will face Gujarat in their next match on Monday (November 16) at the same venue. They will then take on Goa, Vidarbha, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Uttarakhand on November 18, 20, 22, 24 and 26, respectively.

item.title: After his father's death, 49ers' Corliss Waitman found purpose amid his pain
item.description: With the 49ers offense clicking this season, punter Corliss Waitman has punted only 21 times in eight games going into the weekend. (Lindsey Wasson/Associated Press) Corliss Waitman was born in Belgium, grew up in the Netherlands and owns the obscure distinction of being the only left-footed Black player at his position in NFL history. There is, quite literally, no one quite like the San Francisco 49ers punter, but so many can relate to what drove him to the highest level of professional success: He wanted to honor his father. In 2013, Waitman, a senior at Milton (Fla.) High School, was being recruited by Oregon and Auburn, two years after the Ducks and Tigers played in the national championship game. But he passed on the bluebloods. His heart was set on a startup: the University of South Alabama, which began playing football in 2009. Waitman's dad, Jose, played basketball at South Alabama before embarking on a 15-season professional career in Europe. In 1987, he was named MVP of a Dutch league. Jose Waitman, 6-foot-9 and 220 pounds during his playing days, was a towering presence in Corliss' life. He died at 48 on April 17, 2013, when Corliss was 17. Months later, Corliss sent an email to a coach at a fledgling program a year removed from a 2-11 season that didn't know he was interested. He asked if the staff could recruit him. "I went to South Alabama," Corliss said, "solely to honor my dad." During a stellar debut season with the 49ers, Waitman, 31, recently reflected on his improbable journey and the role his father played in it. After signing a one-year deal in March, Waitman ranks fifth in the NFL in net punting average (44.0 yards) and has dropped 47.6% of his kicks inside the 20-yard line, ranking 10th. He was named the NFC Special Teams Player of the Week after pinning all five of his punts inside the 20, including three inside the 10, in the 49ers' 32-29 win at Seattle on Oct. 11. Niners punter Corliss Waitman was named the NFC Special Teams Player of the Week after pinning all five of his punts inside the 20 in a 32-29 win in Seattle on Oct. 11. (Alika Jenner/Getty Images) The honor was another step in Waitman's nomadic NFL career, a journey he didn't see coming. He grew up playing soccer in Europe and was blessed with a bazooka left leg. But when he was introduced to football shortly after arriving in the United States at 14, he was comically inconsistent. He didn't become Milton's full-time punter until his senior season. Waitman quickly ascended to all-state, a transformation that began in the months after his father died from the complications of a stroke. Chafan Marsh, Waitman's high school coach who was close friends with Jose, said Jose's death gave Corliss purpose as he dealt with his pain. item.title: 49ers to face struggling Cowboys defense, but S.F. has concerns as well
item.description: Niners tight end George Kittle, left, and running back Christian McCaffrey could be in line for big games Sunday against a Cowboys defense that ranks near the bottom in the NFL. (Carlos Avila Gonzalez/S.F. Chronicle) Kyle Shanahan vs. Christian Parker. Folks, this doesn't look like a fair fight. Shanahan, the San Francisco 49ers head coach, is in his 19th season as an offensive play-caller. Parker, the Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator, is a rookie in his role. Shanahan has a coaching tree, assistants who have exited and taken his much-imitated system with them. Parker has a coaching assistant who unexpectedly entered this season to help fix Parker's broken system: Dallas brought Mike Pettine out of retirement last month, making the former NFL head coach and coordinator a defensive assistant. Remember the 49ers' 38-17 win last weekend over the Raiders and their disastrous defense? Sunday could be the sequel when the 49ers visit the Cowboys, owners of a group that ranks 31st in the NFL in rushing yards allowed, 30th in total yards, 28th in yards per play, 25th in points and, well, there's more, but you get the idea. The 49ers were asked this week why one of the NFL's worst defenses - statistically speaking - could be friskier than expected. "We never look at a team's stats," offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak said. "We don't let that tell us anything. We watch the tape. This is the NFL and, first of all, every team is well-coached. Every team has good players. And we watch the tape, and we see who's out there." The tape does show the Cowboys being gashed on the ground. They have allowed three runs of 40-plus yards, an NFL high, and 11 runs of 20-plus yards, tied for the most in the NFL. What Shanahan has told his players: If you take away all the bad plays by the Cowboys defense, they'd be good. "Coach Shanahan shared with us that - I think they're ranked 31st in run defense - but they've given up (three) 50-yards-plus runs," tight end George Kittle said. "So if you just take off those explosives, they're like a top-12 defense." In fairness to Parker, he inherited a mess. The Cowboys have allowed 20-plus points in 16 straight games, the longest streak in the franchise's 67-season history and the longest in the NFL since the Jaguars had a 25-game stretch from 2019-2021. Niners quarterback Brock Purdy , the leader of a 7-1 team with the NFL's sixth-ranked offense, did note the Cowboys (4-5) aren't winless or sackless, tied for 20th in the league with 17 sacks. "They can make you pay," Purdy said. "They've won games and have gotten quarterbacks in some situations where the quarterbacks had to play ball and be smart." Trouble in the secondary: Covering Cowboys wide receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens presents a challenge for any NFL team. It becomes especially hard for a team that doesn't have its top two cornerbacks. item.title: Report – Juventus Reignite Interest in Tottenham Defender Ahead of January Transfer Window
item.description: Report – Juventus Reignite Interest in Tottenham Defender Ahead of January Transfer Window Juventus have reportedly revived their interest in Tottenham Hotspur left-back Destiny Udogie ahead of the January transfer window. According to Gazzetta dello Sport , the Premier League giants are potentially open to letting the Italian defender leave on loan. Juventus have identified Udogie as a possible solution to their left-back shortage, although the 23-year-old currently sits behind Rayan Ait-Nouri and Alejandro Balde on their shortlist. Luciano Spalletti wants to strengthen his defensive options in January, but securing a deal for Manchester City outcast Ait-Nouri could prove complicated. Balde represents another attractive option. However, Barcelona may not be enthusiastic about losing their academy graduate. Udogie, meanwhile, could offer Juventus a more attainable alternative, particularly with Tottenham reportedly exploring temporary destinations where he can rebuild his confidence and regain match fitness following persistent injury problems. The Italy international has struggled to establish himself as a regular starter in North London this season, making just seven appearances across all competitions. Our take on Juventus & Udogie Juventus could also benefit from their increasingly productive relationship with Spurs. Indeed, they have already signed Guglielmo Vicario and Pape Matar Sarr through recent loan agreements. Udogie could follow in their footsteps in January after tumbling down the pecking order under Roberto De Zerbi. His Italian nationality would represent another advantage as the Turin giants navigate financial restrictions and squad-registration requirements. Although no agreement appears imminent, Udogie’s situation remains one to monitor as Juventus weigh up their options before the winter window opens.

item.title: ‘He lied to me!’ – Former Marseille sporting director Mehdi Benatia blasts former chairman Pablo Longoria
item.description: ‘He lied to me!’ – Former Marseille sporting director Mehdi Benatia blasts former chairman Pablo Longoria Whilst Olympique de Marseille have seen a resurgence in results in recent weeks, the upcoming winter transfer window could cause further headaches for the club’s management. Having failed to sign a single player last summer, the Marseille-based club is likely to be forced once again to cut costs and trim its squad to meet the requirements of the French financial regulator. This is a tricky situation, which OM’s former sporting director Mehdi Benatia has commented on, pointing the finger at his former president Pablo Longoria for the club’s predicament. “The coach (Roberto De Zerbi) thought that in January we’d have €30 million to spend on signings, to bring in a top striker,” the former Juventus player said in an interview with Canal+ . “When I told him, ‘Coach, you’ve got it wrong – we need to bring in 35 million euros!’ , he said, ‘What?! But that’s not what I was told!’ Well, no – neither was I!” When asked again about feeling tricked by Longoria, Benatia replied bluntly: “He lied to me, that’s for sure. I’m saying it on TV: he lied to me. Of course he lied to me!” These comments certainly help us understand a little better how Marseille ended up in the situation they find themselves in today. item.title: Watch: Barcelona captain Raphinha sent off alongside Ancelotti after Brazil defeat against Japan
item.description: Watch: Barcelona captain Raphinha sent off alongside Ancelotti after Brazil defeat against Japan Raphinha endured a frustrating evening in Singapore as Brazil lost 3-2 to Japan on November 14, with the Barcelona captain receiving a straight red card alongside head coach Carlo Ancelotti following protests over Japan’s stoppage-time winner. The dismissal came just weeks after the forward’s comments about managing his international workload sparked controversy in Brazil. Raphinha had recently returned from a muscle problem and admitted during his contract renewal ceremony that he was not yet fully fit. Although he subsequently clarified his comments, his involvement against Japan has renewed attention on the club’s concerns about his physical condition. Raphinha starts despite concerns over his fitness Barcelona had reason to be cautious about Raphinha’s involvement after he suffered repeated muscular problems during recent international windows. Following his contract extension until 2030, the forward explained that he had spoken with Ancelotti about looking after his physical condition. However, his comments were interpreted by some as a request to limit his playing time. Raphinha addressed that controversy at a press conference in Singapore, insisting that he wanted to represent Brazil whenever he was physically capable. He explained that his intention was to avoid further injuries, not to dictate which matches he should play. Ancelotti selected the Barcelona forward in the starting line-up against Japan, deploying him centrally as Brazil’s number nine. Ultimately, Raphinha was replaced by Endrick in the 71st minute, having contributed 39 touches, two shots on target and one clear chance created. Japan comeback ends with controversial red cards Brazil struggled defensively and conceded twice inside the opening 19 minutes through Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura. Raphinha was sent off against Japan for protesting. (Photo by Ashok Kumar/Getty Images) Vinicius Jr. brought Brazil back into the contest with two goals, equalising in the 75th minute after his first strike had reduced the deficit. Japan nevertheless secured victory through Tatsuhiro Sakamoto’s stoppage-time goal. Brazil’s players and coaching staff protested over a possible foul on Joao Gomes during the build-up, with Raphinha and Ancelotti both receiving straight red cards. The result leaves Raphinha with an unwanted disciplinary incident to accompany an already difficult international break. His dismissal also means Brazil will need to assess his availability for their next friendly against Singapore on November 17.

item.title: Liverpool set to make decision on forward move in January
item.description: Liverpool set to make decision on forward move in January Liverpool January Transfer Plans Take Shape with Djylian N’Guessan and Will Wright in Focus Liverpool’s next transfer window has already begun to come into view, and one piece of business is effectively in place before January even arrives. As Liverpool Echo reports, the club are due to complete the permanent arrival of Djylian N’Guessan from Saint-Etienne for £4.25 million when the winter market opens. It is an interesting development, particularly because it says plenty about how Liverpool’s recruitment department are trying to balance immediate needs with medium-term planning. N’Guessan, 18, has spent the first half of the campaign on loan with Brest, where minutes have been hard to come by. That lack of game time will naturally be part of Liverpool’s review once he officially joins, especially with Andoni Iraola and club staff assessing how best to handle a young forward still early in his development. There was at least an encouraging reminder of his potential during the international break. N’Guessan scored on his France Under-19 debut in a 6-0 win over Norway, another positive marker for a player whose youth record already stands out. His previous output for France at Under-16 and Under-17 level, along with his impact at the 2025 European Under-17 Championship, underlines why Liverpool moved early to secure him. Photo: IMAGO What happens next may have a wider effect inside the academy structure. Liverpool are expected to assess N’Guessan’s immediate pathway in January, and that could influence the situation of Will Wright. The 18-year-old has been one of the standout performers in the youth ranks this season, producing 13 goals in 12 appearances across Premier League 2, the EFL Trophy and the UEFA Youth League. Wright’s numbers have demanded attention. Six goals in the UEFA Youth League, including hat-tricks against LASK and Fenerbahce, have elevated his profile further, and his England Under-19 debut this week offered another sign that his progress is being noticed beyond Kirkby. This is where Liverpool’s winter planning becomes particularly compelling. N’Guessan arrives with pedigree and a transfer fee attached, Wright has momentum and form, and Iraola now has decisions to make over whether development is best served through internal promotion, a loan move, or a reshuffle of opportunities across the club’s young attacking options. January may not bring the biggest Liverpool headline of the season, but this is still a window that could shape the next phase for two highly-rated forwards. item.description: Credit: Rob Gray-Imagn Images Utah enters Saturday as the only unbeaten team left in the Big 12, sitting at 9-0 while Arizona fights to keep its own story alive at 7-2. item.description: Florida Atlantic's football game at Tulsa on Saturday was pushed back to a 7:15 start in the aftermath of Friday's FAA-ordered grounding of all flights in the United States. According to a press release from the university, the Owls were scheduled to depart on Saturday morning. Kickoff originally was scheduled for 3:30 p.m. "We are very appreciative of the American Conference and our colleagues at Tulsa for their communication and accommodations during these unique circumstances," said Josh McCowan, FAU's Vice President and Director of Athletics. The FAA cited extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns related to an air traffic control issue when announcing the grounding. The directive ordered all departing aircraft to remain grounded until further notice and the ground stop remained in effect until around 8 p.m. The Owls , who were waiting on buses on the tarmac when the order came down, eventually returned to campus. Florida Atlantic was not the only Florida college football team affected by the grounding. Central Florida's home game against Arizona State was pushed back to a 5:30 p.m. start (from 3:30) due to the Sun Devils flight also being grounded on Friday. Other sports events around the nation also were affected. The FAU-Tulsa game will air live on ESPN+ and can also be heard on Fox Sports South Florida 640 a.m. This article originally appeared on Palm Beach Post: Florida Atlantic expected to fly to Tulsa, football game moved to 7:15

item.title: Spalletti’s three January transfer priorities for Juventus revealed
item.description: Spalletti’s three January transfer priorities for Juventus revealed La Gazzetta dello Sport reports that Luciano Spalletti’s three transfer priorities for the January transfer window are a ‘classic’ centre-forward, a central midfielder and a left-back. The Bianconeri are struggling this season, sitting seventh in Serie A with just 18 points from 11 league games. ITALY – OCTOBER 25: Head coach of Juventus FC Luciano Spalletti looks on ahead the Serie A match between US Lecce and Juventus at Stadio Via del Mare on October 25, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Maurizio Lagana/Getty Images) Coach Spalletti has been dealing with a deep injury crisis since the start of the season, being forced to cope without Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram and Manuel Locatelli, among others, for several months. And it’s no surprise that one of Spalletti’s priorities in the January window is to sign a new central midfielder. According to Gazzetta, the top three names on the Bianconeri’s agenda are Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg (Marseille), Darryl Bakola (Sassuolo) and Italy international Issa Doumbia. LISBON, PORTUGAL – SEPTEMBER 9: Issa Doumbia of Sporting CP celebrates a third goal scored by Rodrigo Zalazar of Sporting CP in action during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Sporting Club de Portugal and Galatasaray A.S. at Estadio Jose Alvalade on September 9, 2026 in Lisbon, Portugal. (Photo by Carlos Rodrigues/Getty Images) The former Venezia midfielder joined Sporting CP for €20m last summer, and Gazzetta describes him as a ‘dream signing’ for the Old Lady, suggesting a January move is unlikely. Spalletti’s starting point, however, will be to welcome a new, classic centre-forward, with Alexander Sorloth (Atletico Madrid), Folarin Balogun (Monaco) and Mateo Retegui among the Bianconeri’s top targets. LEEDS, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 04: Destiny Udogie of Tottenham Hotspur is challenged by Brenden Aaronson of Leeds United during the Premier League match between Leeds United and Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road on October 04, 2025 in Leeds, England. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) Gazzetta, however, notes that convincing Al Qadisiah to sell Retegui might be difficult in January. As for the defence and the left-back role specifically, Juve’s three top names are Rayan Aït-Nouri (Manchester City), Destiny Udogie (Tottenham) and Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde, again described as a dream target for the Serie A giants.

item.title: Chris Long says Justin Jefferson is ‘wasting his career’ with the Minnesota Vikings after what’s been happening
item.description: Photo by David Berding/Getty Images Chris Long has suggested that the Minnesota Vikings’ poor quarterback options in recent years mean that Justin Jefferson has been wasting his career. The Vikings are 6-2 for the season and their defence has largely carried them to that positive record as their offence has been pretty poor. Carson Wentz has struggled when selected and even when Kyler Murray starts, Minnesota don’t look that impressive going forward. Now, speaking on ‘Green Light with Chris Long’ , Long has suggested that Jefferson is ‘wasting his career’ due to the lack of quality quarterback options the Vikings have had. He suggested that of eight recent QBs they have used, most of them have been poor and in turn, Justin ‘hasn’t gotten the ball with 17 quarterback changes’. Long explained: “Justin Jefferson, who, to me, is one of the most likeable, respectable superstars in the NFL, and especially even-keeled for a skilled guy. You know, guys who lose their minds when they don’t get the ball. “This guy hasn’t gotten the ball with 17 quarterback changes. I mean, with Darnold, there was that one year, but that was the stat: 17 quarterback changes since Kirk Cousins left. That’s eight different quarterbacks, by my count. And most of them have been dog water, and he’s wasting his career.” But the Vikings and Jefferson may now be hoping that the return of Kirk Cousins can help them improve a great deal on the offence. Cousins last played for the Vikings in 2023, managing 2,331 passing yards in eight games that season. item.title: FAA ground stop could impact Browns vs. Texans, rest of Week 10 in a big way
item.description: When it comes to things of importance, sports might be much lower on the totem pole than many of us devoted fans realize or even think about. Friday’s FAA ground stop to all outgoing flights was an example of a real-world issue impacting many people in many ways, but it could also impact the world of sports. Many college games on Saturday were still up in the air late Friday night into Saturday morning due to the grounding. As flights got back going after 9 PM on Friday, how airlines and systems would prioritize the restart was something important to watch. “Smaller movements will take a lower priority,” with football teams encouraged to contact the FAA to try to get their flights scheduled. The Houston Texans are still in Texas early Saturday morning. While there is unlikely to be an issue with them getting to Cleveland to face the Browns, it is possible that their schedule will be impacted, including the team’s normal Saturday walkthrough. That will likely be true for all visiting teams this week. The bigger impact on the field could come from the officials for the game. Unlike teams, referees do not travel on a specific charter that can be organized with the FAA. College officials have already raised concerns about their officials making it to their destinations: The numbers are staggering : 12,506 flights have been cancelled so far between yesterday and today, per Flight Aware. The number is expected to grow throughout the day. On Saturday morning already, 3,374 flights have been canceled and 1,008 are delayed nationwide, per FlightAware. In the NFL, like college, refs generally have full-time jobs doing other things throughout the week, and most are scheduled to work most or every weekend. While the NFL generally has backup plans, getting enough officials to their right spots might be tough given the above numbers. Visiting teams could be impacted by the FAA ground stop, but all games could see an impact in how many officials are assigned and in what position those officials are assigned on Sunday. Something for fans to remember if/when a big call does or doesn’t go the Browns’ way.

item.title: Watch: Under-fire Real Madrid forward scores stunning brace in 2-3 international loss to Japan
item.description: Watch: Under-fire Real Madrid forward scores stunning brace in 2-3 international loss to Japan Vinicius Jr. delivered an encouraging individual performance for Brazil on Saturday, scoring twice in their 2-3 friendly defeat against Japan in Singapore. The Real Madrid forward produced two impressive finishes to bring his country back from a two-goal deficit, offering a timely reminder of his attacking quality amid questions surrounding his form this season. As far as the game is concerned, Japan took control early through Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura, who scored in the 15th and 19th minutes respectively. Brazil struggled to contain their opponents during the opening stages, but Vinicius provided the response with a long-range strike in the 33rd minute before finding the net again in the 75th minute to restore parity. Vinicius gives Brazil a route back into the contest Brazil’s comeback owed much to the Real Madrid forward’s individual quality. His first goal came from a powerful effort from outside the penalty area that found the top corner, giving Brazil a much-needed foothold in the contest. The second was another demonstration of his ability to threaten from distance, as Vinicius produced a low finish in the 75th minute to make it 2-2, completing his brace and putting Brazil in a position to turn the match around. The two goals were particularly encouraging for a player who has faced scrutiny over his performances at club level . Indeed, one international appearance cannot resolve questions about his consistency, but scoring twice against Japan is certainly a positive step in his attempt to regain confidence and sharpness. Japan punish Brazil after late controversy Despite Vinicius’s contribution, Brazil could not complete the comeback. Japan continued to threaten and found the decisive goal in the 91st minute through Tatsuhiro Sakamoto, who converted after Brazil failed to deal with the situation inside their penalty area. The goal provoked furious protests from the Brazilian players and coaching staff, who believed there had been a foul in the build-up. Those reactions resulted in straight red cards for head coach Carlo Ancelotti and Raphinha. The Barcelona forward had already been substituted, but was still dismissed following the protests.

The Spartan junior seems to have made the best decision, as Izzo already sees a bright future for his guard. Fears started his junior season efficiently, scoring 13 points and adding 11 assists in a 96-59 win over Quinnipiac. But in the last two games, his offense cooled down as his shooting percentage dropped and turnovers increased, prompting Izzo to hold a long meeting with his player, who vowed to respond. “I’d have to say that I had a long meeting with Jeremy this morning, and he vowed what he was going to do, and he might have had his best game as a Spartan,” Izzo told reporters after the win over Northern Iowa . “He might have had the best game of anybody. The way he ran the team, the way he shot the ball, the way he scored it. Nine assists, no turnovers, should have had a couple more assists. item.description: PSG midfielder Fabián Ruiz reveals he ‘would like to end’ his career at Real Betis Fabián Ruiz (30) has never made a secret of his attachment to Real Betis. Having come through the Andalusian club’s academy, the Spanish midfielder cut his teeth there, eventually making his professional debut in 2014, at a time when Los Béticos were still playing in the second division. After moving to Napoli in 2018, Ruiz made a name for himself there, before truly coming into his own whilst playing for Paris Saint-Germain, where he won every possible title, and establishing himself in the national team, with whom he notably won the World Cup last summer. Now aged 30, the Los Palacios y Villafranca native has clearly not forgotten his roots. And eight years after leaving the club where he spent 14 years of his life, Ruiz hopes one day to have the opportunity to wear their colours once again. “I’d like to finish my career there, spend my final years at Betis, back home,” he told Spanish media outlet Okdiario . “I hope that will happen one day and that I’ll be able to wear the Betis shirt again.” GFFN | Léo Aschi

item.title: ‘This kid’: Draymond Green says he just cannot allow Yaxel Lendeborg to do one thing during Warriors games
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Draymond Green is having to be a good older brother to his Golden State Warriors teammate Yaxel Lendeborg on and off the court. The 36-year-old is one of the most experienced players on the roster, and along with Steph Curry, he is a leader in the locker room. Lendeborg, who is still a rookie, has a lot to learn, not just about the game but how to behave in heated moments as well. Green is doing his best to teach that to his young teammate. Draymond Green says he cannot allow Yaxel Lendeborg to fight during games Lendeborg wears his heart on his sleeve every time, and that gets him into altercations. What happened with Luka Doncic made the headlines, and he has since had a few scuffles with other players too in the middle of games. Green, who has seen and been involved in such incidents more than most others, has claimed that he cannot allow Lendeborg to get into fights and has urged the rookie to leave them for players like him. Green said on his podcast : “I’ve got to stay on the court with him because that kid is about to be a star. I can’t be having him fighting out there. I take on those battles. I can’t be letting my young fella (get into fights). “I love that you on that type of time, but that’s why we’re here, you know. Guys out there, when they come touch you, we’re coming to do that, you know? I got to get him to understand that, too, like: ‘Hey, man, always keep that attitude, but let us come handle that, man. You get over here.’ “Like, we ain’t letting Steph fight. Steph got to get over here. Here we go. You know, so like move over here, young fella. Let us handle that. That’s why some of us are here, young fella, so you’ve got to reel it in a little bit now.” Lendeborg really is a star in the making, and he has all the talent and ability in the world to become one of the biggest names in the NBA. But right now, the 24-year-old needs to be protected, and experienced players like Green and Curry are doing what they need to do to keep him on the right path. That really is great to see, and it should help Lendeborg focus on what’s important, which is fulfilling his massive potential.
